key_insight: A slice-wise synthetic reasoning dataset can teach a 2D-pretrained multimodal model stronger 3D spatial reasoning for medical imaging without native 3D pretraining.
clinical_relevance: This could improve interpretable volumetric image understanding in clinical workflows by better reflecting how radiologists track findings across slices.
method: Built a large structured reasoning dataset from 3D scans using slice-wise synthesis.
Converted global clinical priors into per-slice observations and a Chain-of-Thought rationale.
Instruction-tuned a standard 2D-pretrained MLLM on the synthesized data to boost volumetric comprehension.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports significant gains across multiple 3D medical benchmarks, with the tuned model rivaling more resource-intensive native 3D architectures.
watch_item: Because the reasoning is synthesized rather than directly annotated, performance and interpretability may depend on how faithfully the generated CoT matches real clinical reasoning.
paper_title: Towards Enhancing 3D Spatial Reasoning in Medical Multimodal Large Language Models
